title: Quantum LDPC Codes from Polynomial Minors
authors: Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell
abstract: We construct quantum codes from codewords of a cyclic code and the minors of a polynomial matrix. The construction uses a two-row, three-column matrix whose minors yield a second matrix satisfying the CSS orthogonality condition. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors. A residue characterization identifies additional common factors of the minors and leads to a method for controlling the dimension through polynomial selection. We also give a condition for changing the minor generator without changing the code. Explicit polynomial constructions yield 13 quantum codes with verified minimum distances, including a $[[255,80,12]]$ code of rate $80/255$.
summary: This paper develops a method to construct Quantum LDPC codes by leveraging the minors of a polynomial matrix within the CSS framework. The authors derive formulas to precisely control the code dimension and provide explicit constructions, yielding codes like $[[255, 80, 12]]$. This work offers a powerful algebraic tool for designing robust quantum error correction codes.
main_problem: The paper focuses on constructing quantum error-correcting codes, specifically Quantum LDPC codes, using algebraic structures derived from polynomial minors.
main_result: The authors successfully construct explicit quantum codes, including a verified example with parameters $[[255, 80, 12]]$, by controlling the code dimension through polynomial selection.
method: The construction utilizes the CSS framework, generating stabilizer generators from the minors of a specialized two-row, three-column polynomial matrix $H(x)$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum error-correcting code itself, defined by its stabilizer generators derived from polynomial algebra over finite fields, leading to codes of length $3N$.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, code dimension $k$, and minimum distance $d$.
important_parameters: The length $n$ is $3N$, and the dimension $k$ is derived from GCDs of polynomial minors.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the CSS orthogonality condition and specific theorems regarding the rank of matrices formed by polynomial minors.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables listing parameters and polynomials for constructed codes, detailing row weights and minimum distances for various examples.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the construction using polynomial minors and the CSS condition, derives dimension formulas based on GCDs, and concludes with explicit examples and discussions on controlling parameters.
why_interesting: The rigorous algebraic construction of quantum codes using polynomial minors provides a powerful, systematic tool for generating new, high-performance quantum error-correcting codes.
